elements.name: Hydrogen
elements.note: The lightest atom of all — most hydrogen nuclei are a single proton.

elements.name: Helium
elements.note: Shell 1 is completely full — that is why helium refuses to react.

elements.name: Lithium
elements.note: One lonely electron in shell 2 — lithium hands it away easily.

elements.name: Beryllium
elements.note: Two protons, two neutrons, two shell-2 electrons — tidy pairs.

elements.name: Boron
elements.note: Three electrons in shell 2 make boron a builder of odd structures.

elements.name: Carbon
elements.note: Four bindable electrons — the backbone of every living thing.

elements.name: Nitrogen
elements.note: 78% of the air you are breathing is nitrogen atoms.

elements.name: Oxygen
elements.note: Two electrons short of a full shell — oxygen grabs electrons.

elements.name: Fluorine
elements.note: One electron short of full — the most reactive non-metal.

elements.name: Neon
elements.note: A sealed shell 2 — neon glows alone and reacts with no one.

elements.name: Sodium
elements.note: That single shell-3 electron is why sodium is desperate to react.

elements.name: Magnesium
elements.note: Two outer electrons — the green heart of every chlorophyll leaf.

elements.name: Aluminium
elements.note: Light, shiny and third in shell 3 — foil and aeroplanes.

elements.name: Silicon
elements.note: Half a shell to share — the skeleton of sand, glass and chips.

elements.name: Phosphorus
elements.note: Carries energy in every cell — strike-anywhere chemistry.

elements.name: Sulfur
elements.note: Yellow crystals of eight atoms — the smell of volcanoes.

elements.name: Chlorine
elements.note: One electron short of full — a fierce electron thief.

elements.name: Argon
elements.note: Shell 3 full under the simple rule — a calm, lazy gas.

elements.name: Potassium
elements.note: One electron far from home — bananas and nerve signals.

elements.name: Calcium
elements.note: Two shell-4 electrons — bones, shells and limestone.
